items.title: Dynamic array
items.prompt: Implement a dynamic array class with append, pop, get, and len, backed by a fixed-size list you resize yourself. State the amortized cost of append and prove it in two sentences.
items.rubric: Doubling strategy, amortized O(1) argument, correct resize, bounds checks.

items.title: Hash map with chaining
items.prompt: Implement a hash map (get, put, delete) using separate chaining, with resizing when the load factor passes 0.75. Explain how a bad hash function hurts you and what Python's dict does differently.
items.rubric: Buckets of lists, hash and modulo, rehash on grow, load factor, open addressing mention.

items.title: Min-heap
items.prompt: Implement a binary min-heap with push, pop, and peek on a plain list. Give the complexity of each and explain sift-up and sift-down.
items.rubric: Index arithmetic (2i+1, 2i+2), sift operations, O(log n), heapify O(n) bonus.

items.title: Singly linked list
items.prompt: Implement a singly linked list with push_front, push_back, delete(value), and reverse() in place. Explain the two-pointer reversal.
items.rubric: Node class, careful pointer updates, reverse with prev/cur/next, handles empty and single node.

items.title: LRU cache
items.prompt: Implement an LRU cache with O(1) get and put using a hash map plus a doubly linked list, without OrderedDict. Walk through what happens on a hit, a miss, and an eviction.
items.rubric: Sentinel head/tail, move-to-front, evict from tail, map from key to node.

items.title: Trie
items.prompt: Implement a trie with insert, search, and starts_with. Then add a method that returns all words with a given prefix. Discuss memory cost and when a trie beats a hash set.
items.rubric: Node with children dict and end flag, DFS for prefix listing, memory trade-off.

items.title: Union-find
items.prompt: Implement disjoint sets with path compression and union by rank. Explain the near-constant amortized cost and use it to count connected components in an edge list.
items.rubric: find with compression, union by rank/size, inverse Ackermann mention, components count.

items.title: BFS and DFS on a grid
items.prompt: Write BFS (shortest path length) and DFS (reachability) on a grid of 0/1 cells where 1 is a wall. Explain when you pick each and why BFS uses a queue.
items.rubric: Visited set, 4-direction moves, queue vs stack/recursion, O(rows*cols).

items.title: Dijkstra
items.prompt: Implement Dijkstra's algorithm with a heap for a weighted graph given as an adjacency list. Explain why it fails with negative edges and name what you would use instead.
items.rubric: Lazy deletion with (dist, node) heap, relaxation, O((V+E) log V), Bellman-Ford mention.

items.title: Topological sort
items.prompt: Implement Kahn's algorithm for topological order and detect a cycle. Give a real use (build systems, course prerequisites) and complexity.
items.rubric: In-degree counts, queue of zero in-degree, cycle if output shorter than V, O(V+E).

items.title: Binary search variants
items.prompt: Write lower_bound and upper_bound on a sorted list, then use lower_bound to solve 'first bad version'. Explain the invariant that stops off-by-one bugs.
items.rubric: Half-open interval invariant, lo/hi updates, returns insertion points.

items.title: Quicksort and merge sort
items.prompt: Implement merge sort and quicksort. Compare stability, worst case, memory, and which one Python's sort is related to.
items.rubric: Correct recursion, pivot choice, O(n log n) average, quicksort worst case, Timsort mention.

items.title: Sliding window maximum
items.prompt: Implement the maximum of every window of size k over an array in O(n) using a deque. Explain the invariant the deque keeps.
items.rubric: Monotonic decreasing deque of indices, pop front when out of window, amortized O(1).

items.title: Bloom filter
items.prompt: Implement a Bloom filter with k hash functions over a bit array. Explain false positives, why there are no false negatives, and how to size it for 1M items at 1% error.
items.rubric: Bit array, multiple hashes, add/might_contain, sizing formula m and k.

items.title: Rate limiter data structure
items.prompt: Implement a token bucket class with allow(now) that refills at r tokens per second up to capacity c. Then show how you would shard it per user and what breaks when the clock jumps.
items.rubric: Lazy refill on access, float tokens, monotonic clock, per-key map, clock skew note.

items.title: Consistent hashing ring
items.prompt: Implement a consistent hashing ring with virtual nodes: add_node, remove_node, get_node(key). Explain how many keys move when a node joins and why virtual nodes help.
items.rubric: Sorted ring with bisect, virtual node replicas, ~1/n keys move, balance.
